meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here? Owen's zero. Start there.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what did you have when you entered it?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Go on. Start with whatever you can put in front of me.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for acting against a student. What else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then why did you lead with it? Put the rest in front of me.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
"Quite different" is an adjective. A timed paragraph in a classroom and an essay written over days will always look different. Show me both pieces, and tell me what exactly differs.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
I didn't ask what you think of him. I asked what differs between the two pieces.
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. What does the essay argue, and where in it can I see the difference?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
A different argument isn't a crime. Do you have that outline with you? I want it next to the essay.
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
Which one doesn't? And you haven't answered me: do you have the outline with you?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
You've skipped my question about the outline twice now. What did Owen say on November 2, and did you write it down that day?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
"Being stuck" is not wrong. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot after class gives a short answer. Where are your notes from that conversation?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
That's what you say he said. Did you write it down that day, yes or no?
I wrote notes that same day.
Okay. Then I want those notes and the outline on paper, not described. Ten minutes.
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Put them on the table, both of them, and the essay beside them.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
You gave him a zero. Show me the notes and the outline.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years isn't a document. Owen isn't "this." Notes, outline, essay: on the table, Hale.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
No, you're not. Start with the one piece of paper you trust most.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
"Something." Which quotation, and what exactly is wrong with it? Tell me where I can look it up myself.
Let me find the page, sorry.
Two minutes. Find it.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Students misquote, or lift a line from a study guide and cite it wrong. What edition did you check, and did you search the whole play or just that scene?
I checked three editions.
Okay, Hale. Is anything on his record right now?
So that's what I have.
That isn't what I asked. Is anything on his record, yes or no?
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
I haven't moved. Is there anything on his record, or isn't there?
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
Then say it. What does it show, and at what times?
What if we talked about a rewrite?
A rewrite for what? You said there was version history, and I haven't seen it yet.
I'm trying to help him.
Helping him is the zero coming off. Version history, Hale, with times.
Why won't you just listen?
I've listened for twenty minutes. You've told me a checker score, a quotation, and an outline you haven't shown me. Put the version history on the table.
Okay. I'm sorry.
My call is waiting. You have one minute. Whatever happens, nothing goes on his record and nobody hears about it.
Can I call you tomorrow?
No. You have a minute, and you're spending it asking me for more time.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
The version history. Every time on it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, nothing placed on Owen's record, and every document you rely on sent to me in full. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She got to her fallback position, that nothing goes on his record and it stays quiet, and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero off and your documents on paper. That is not the fair outcome, since you never committed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 with the new mark replacing the zero, and her time ran out first.
What moved her: Telling her you had checked three editions of the play for the line you called made up, because she could verify it herself, and that moved her off her opening demand.
What cost ground: Raising a rewrite before you had shown the version history, because it let her ask what the rewrite was for and you never got to your strongest document.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night, since you named the version history but never gave a single time from it. It proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what the version history showed and at what times, answer with the exact times and edits, and only then offer the 4.4 rewrite with a date that protects the December 1 deadline.
